the molecular basis of Cry11Ba action on A. gambie larva, and provides new insights into the molecular basis of insecticidal Cry toxin action on mosquitoes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Cry11Ba is a multi-receptor toxin.
the binding of Cry11Ba with AgAmy1 and/or Agm3 on the BBMV of A. gambie larva midguts is the primary event for Cry11Ba toxicity.
AgCad2, AgAPN2, AgALP1, AgAmy1 and m3 are the receptors for Cry11Ba in the larval mid-gut of A. gambaie, and they are the key to the toxicity of this toxin to A. gambie larvae.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Cry11Ba toxicity depends on at least five receptors, AgCad2, AgAmy1, Agm3, AgAPN2 and AgALP1, on A. gambi
the Cry11Ba toxin has at least 4 different receptors on the larval mid-gut epithelial cells, which may be responsible for its high toxicity to A. gammabie.

the GPI-anchored α-amylase AgAmy1 and α-glucosiadse Agm3 are involved in regulation of the toxicity of Cry11Ba on Anopheles larvae.
